key_insight: Biot–Savart-inspired activation functions improve incompressible-flow PINN accuracy while preserving the standard velocity–pressure formulation.
engineering_relevance: Flow-informed neural representations could improve simulation accuracy for wakes, vortices, and localized shear structures.
method: Extract a smooth rational activation from a regularized Biot–Savart kernel.
Test fixed and learnable kernel-scale variants.
Retain conventional physics-informed training to isolate activation effects.
evidence_signal: Across five flow benchmarks and 21 benchmark–architecture comparisons, fixed- and learnable-scale variants consistently reduced combined velocity error versus tanh PINNs, with mean relative reductions of 31.7% and 33.2%, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish computational-cost advantages or generalization beyond the tested benchmarks and architectures.
paper_title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
